result.summary: Click analytics per the approved impact analysis: click_events table (V2), best-effort click recording on redirect, private stats endpoint, click erasure on delete under a row lock

decisions.choice: Click recording and deletion both take a PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock on the link row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE); recording only inserts if the link is not deleted
decisions.rationale: Impact risk 3: a click committed after deletion erased the link's clicks would violate the erase-on-delete decision. Concurrent redirects of one link briefly serialize on that lock, acceptable for a single node

decisions.choice: ClickRecorder runs in its own transaction after the redirect lookup; RedirectController catches any RuntimeException from it and still returns the 302
decisions.rationale: NFR1 and the owner's decision that redirect reliability comes first; a failed click is logged by exception type only

decisions.choice: resolveForRedirect(String) keeps its signature (now delegating to resolve(String)), so existing callers and tests keep working
decisions.rationale: FR4 and minimal churn for the existing suite; LinkService does gain a ClickEventRepository constructor argument, so LinkServiceTest setup must be updated in the test stage

decisions.choice: click_date is stored as the UTC day at write time; stats query days >= today-29 and zero-fill in Java, oldest first
decisions.rationale: Time-zone-stable grouping, bounded indexed query, exactly 30 entries (FR2/AC2)

decisions.choice: click_events holds only id, link_id, clicked_at, click_date; the request is never inspected for analytics
decisions.rationale: NFR2 and the owner's no-unique-visitors decision; nothing to profile visitors with

decisions.choice: V2__create_click_events.sql adds the table, a foreign key to links and two indexes; V1 untouched. Verified by upgrading a real v1 database: existing links and tombstones unaffected
decisions.rationale: Forward-only Flyway convention and the upgrade path existing deployments will take
